Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

Our Support team serves as the vital link between our technology ecosystem (Theatro) and our users. We are dedicated to resolving technical issues, answering hardware and network questions, and helping to provide exceptional user satisfaction so our customers can focus on what matters most.


Job Description

At Motorola Solutions, everything starts with our people, and we empower each and every Motorolan to do their best work to protect what matters most. As a Technical Support Representative, you will work within our Customer Support organization providing crucial technical support services to help resolve user inquiries quickly and efficiently. In this role, you will investigate and troubleshoot hardware, software, and networking issues over the phone or through wearable communication platforms.

You will act as an internal liaison to help ensure seamless issue resolution by collaborating with internal technology engineers, Tier 3 support teams, and developers. By accurately logging and tracking service requests through systems like Zendesk, you will help to provide operational rhythm, clarity, and continuous communication across all support activities. Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience is valued as you navigate complex situations and deliver solutions in a dynamic environment.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Troubleshooting & User Support

  • Investigate, diagnose, and resolve technical issues related to hardware operations, software applications, and Wi-Fi or networking infrastructure

  • Walk users through step-by-step troubleshooting processes over the phone and via wearable communicator devices to achieve rapid resolution

  • Log, track, and maintain comprehensive service request histories through the Zendesk support platform across the complete issue lifecycle

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Escalation

  • Collaborate and escalate complex technical challenges to Tier 3 service teams, software developers, and technology engineers

  • Serve as an internal liaison keeping lines of communication clear and flowing between internal engineering teams and external partners

  • Establish and refine internal support processes to help provide seamless, end-to-end issue resolution

Operational Execution & Process Priority

  • Multi-task and set daily priorities effectively in a fast-paced, high-performing operational environment

  • Translate complex technical terms and solutions into accessible language for both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Approach support challenges with initiative, adaptability, and an inclusive perspective to evaluate situations from multiple points of view


Basic Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent

  • 1+ year of experience in a customer service position

Job Requirements

Technical Expertise

  • Networking Infrastructure to analyze and diagnose issues relating to networking hardware, Wi-Fi connectivity, and wearable communicator hardware or software applications

  • Support System Proficiency to document, manage, and analyze service request lifecycles using Zendesk or similar ticketing systems

  • Computer Skills to navigate MS Office Suite and specialized technical troubleshooting tools efficiently

  • Language Proficiency to demonstrate an excellent command of English and Spanish (verbal and written) to clearly explain technical solutions to diverse stakeholders

Professional Experience

  • Shift Availability & Adaptability to maintain reliable attendance and flexibility across 1st shift, 2nd shift, and weekend operational hours

  • Customer Support Operations to investigate technical inquiries, drive workflow rhythm, and deliver timely status updates

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration to partner across engineering, developer, and Tier 3 teams to help resolve escalated technical issues

  • Multitasking & Prioritization to execute tasks, set priorities, and adapt independently or as part of a team in a fast-paced environment

Preferred Qualifications (Optional)

  • Prior experience with hardware operations, wearable tech devices, or wireless communications support


Travel Requirements

None


Relocation Provided

None


Position Type

New Grad

Referral Payment Plan

Yes

EEO Statement

Motorola Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally-protected characteristic.

We are proud of our people-first and community-focused culture, empowering every Motorolan to be their most authentic self and to do their best work to deliver on the promise of a safer world. If you’d like to join our team but feel that you don’t quite meet all of the preferred skills, we’d still love to hear why you think you’d be a great addition to our team.

raw.excerpt: About MedReview MedReview is a leading provider of payment integrity solutions that help national and regional health plans promote population health, ensure payment accuracy, reduce administrative waste, improve provider relationships, and optimize financial performance.
raw.description:
About MedReview

MedReview is a leading provider of payment integrity solutions that help national and regional health plans promote population health, ensure payment accuracy, reduce administrative waste, improve provider relationships, and optimize financial performance. For more than four decades, MedReview has partnered with health plans, third-party administrators, and other healthcare organizations to deliver technology-enabled solutions that identify savings opportunities, drive operational efficiency, and improve healthcare outcomes.

The Opportunity
We are seeking a Senior Physician Reviewer reporting to the Senior Medical Director to serve as a physician leader and clinical subject matter expert for complex payment integrity reviews, clinical validation determinations, DRG validation, readmission reviews, appeals, peer-to-peer discussions, and regulatory complaint resolution. This role provides physician-level judgment on disputed, high-dollar, high-risk, and clinically complex matters and serves as a supervisory and consultative resource to physician reviewers, nurse auditors, coders, quality teams, operations, and client-facing leaders.
The Senior Physician Reviewer applies deep clinical expertise, regulatory knowledge, and payment integrity experience to deliver accurate, defensible, and compliant determinations across Commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and other government-sponsored healthcare programs. The role is critical to maintaining clinical quality, provider credibility, client satisfaction, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities
Clinical Review Leadership
  • Perform complex clinical validation reviews and provide final physician determinations on disputed findings.
  • Review and validate diagnoses, severity of illness, risk adjustment factors, clinical documentation, medical necessity, and reimbursement-related issues.
  • Conduct DRG validation and clinical documentation reviews to confirm accurate assignment and reimbursement.
  • Perform readmission reviews, including assessments of preventability, appropriateness, and documentation support.
  • Review escalated, high-dollar, high-risk, and clinically complex cases requiring physician-level judgment.
  • Provide specialty-specific clinical expertise for inpatient and outpatient payment integrity reviews.

Appeals and Regulatory Management
  • Manage physician-level appeals involving clinical validation, DRG validation, medical necessity, and other payment integrity findings.
  • Conduct peer-to-peer discussions with treating physicians and hospital representatives.
  • Prepare and review clear, evidence-based clinical rationale letters supporting determinations.
  • Participate in external review processes involving providers, health plans, clients, and regulatory agencies.
  • Respond to Medicare complaints, regulatory inquiries, Independent Review Organization requests, and other escalated appeal matters.
  • Provide expert clinical support during litigation, arbitration, audits, or formal dispute resolution activities, as required.

Quality and Compliance
  • Ensure reviews comply with CMS regulations, Medicare guidelines, applicable state requirements, payer policies, clinical criteria, and industry standards.
  • Support quality assurance activities, reviewer calibration, internal audits, and client audit initiatives.
  • Help develop and maintain clinical review policies, methodologies, decision frameworks, and documentation standards.
  • Participate in audit-of-audit programs and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
  • Monitor appeal overturn trends, identify root causes, and recommend improvements to review quality and consistency.

Leadership and Supervision
  • Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and clinical oversight to physician reviewers, nurse reviewers, clinical validation specialists, and appeals staff.
  • Assist with hiring, onboarding, training, calibration, and performance development activities.
  • Support workforce planning, productivity monitoring, quality management, and operational performance.
  • Serve as a clinical consultant to Operations, Account Management, Client Services, Implementation, Quality, Compliance, and executive leadership.
  • Participate in client meetings, operational reviews, and business development activities as a clinical subject matter expert.

Client and Operational Support
  • Present clinical findings, trends, and recommendations to clients and executive stakeholders.
  • Support implementation of new payment integrity programs, review initiatives, and client requirements.
  • Assist with review methodology development, scope expansion, and new program opportunities.
  • Collaborate with coding, analytics, quality, compliance, operations, and technology teams to improve review accuracy, efficiency, and outcomes.

Qualifications

Education and Licensure
  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree from an accredited medical school.
  • Active, unrestricted physician license in at least one U.S. state.
  • Current board certification in an applicable medical specialty.
  • Ability to obtain additional state licenses as business or client needs require.

Experience
  • 10+ years of clinical practice experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in payment integrity, utilization management, revenue cycle, health plan operations, auditing, or healthcare review.
  • Demonstrated physician-level review experience in the areas listed below:
  • Clinical validation and DRG validation
  • Readmission and medical necessity reviews
  • Coding-related clinical reviews
  • Appeals and reconsiderations
  • Peer-to-peer discussions
  • Medicare and regulatory complaint resolution
  • Experience supporting Commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and other government healthcare programs.
  • Prior leadership or supervisory experience supporting physician, nursing, clinical review, or healthcare operations teams.

Knowledge and Skills
  • Expert knowledge in the areas listed below:
  • Clinical Documentation Improvement (CDI)
  • Clinical validation and DRG validation
  • Medicare rules, CMS requirements, and applicable payer policies
  • Payment integrity methodologies and Revenue Cycle Management
  • Medical necessity criteria
  • Appeals, grievances, and regulatory complaint processes
  • Strong understanding of healthcare reimbursement methodologies and payer-provider payment processes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex clinical determinations into clear, defensible rationale.
  • Exceptional provider-relations and peer-to-peer communication skills.
  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to lead and influence cross-functional clinical and operational teams.

Preferred Experience
  • Multi-state physician licensure.
  • Experience serving as a Medical Director, Associate Medical Director, Senior Medical Director, or Senior Physician Advisor.
  • Experience with Recovery Audit Contractor (RAC), Unified Program Integrity Contractor (UPIC), Medicaid Program Integrity, Medicare Advantage, or payment integrity vendors.
  • Certification or advanced training in healthcare quality, utilization management, risk adjustment, patient safety, or healthcare compliance.
  • Experience working with CMS, Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid programs, commercial health plans, third-party administrators, or provider appeals organizations.

What Success Looks LikeWithin the first 12 to 24 months, this role will:
  • Deliver high-quality, evidence-based, and defensible physician determinations while meeting established turnaround times and service-level requirements.
  • Maintain physician reviewer quality scores of 95% or greater.
  • Strengthen appeal defense, improve decision consistency, and reduce avoidable overturns through calibration and root-cause analysis.
  • Ensure timely resolution of escalated provider disputes, peer-to-peer matters, and regulatory complaints.
  • Build reviewer capability through effective coaching, training, and clinical oversight.
  • Improve review methodologies, quality controls, and cross-functional operational processes.
  • Contribute to client satisfaction, program expansion, and MedReview growth initiatives as a credible physician leader.

Compensation - $240,000 - $250,000

Title: SharePoint Developer - WFH
Location: Fully Remote
Experience: 5+ Years
Opportunity: Full-time Employment
Shift: General Shift
Compensation: 12 LPA
Joining: Within two weeks
About the Role
We are looking for an experienced SharePoint Developer to design, develop, customize, and maintain SharePoint Online/SharePoint On‑Premise solutions. The ideal candidate will have strong skills in SharePoint Framework (SPFx), Power Platform, workflows, automation, and integration with Microsoft 365 services.
Key Responsibilities
  • SharePoint Development
  • Design, develop, and implement solutions using SharePoint Online / SharePoint On‑Prem.
  • Build custom components using:
  • SPFx (SharePoint Framework)
  • React / TypeScript / JavaScript
  • CSOM / REST API / Graph API
  • Develop custom web parts, extensions, forms, and solutions.
  • Customize SharePoint pages, site templates, content types, lists, libraries, views, permissions, etc.
  • Power Platform
  • Create Power Apps, Power Automate flows, and Power BI integrations.
  • Automate business processes using workflows and connectors.
  • Integration & Automation
  • Integrate SharePoint with other Microsoft 365 tools (Teams, OneDrive, Outlook, Azure AD).
  • Maintain and develop workflows (Nintex/Power Automate).
  • API-based integrations with external systems.
  • Administration & Support
  • Support site creation, governance, permissions, and content management.
  • Troubleshoot issues, optimize performance, and provide technical support to users.
  • Create documentation, UAT support, and deployment guides.
  • Collaboration
  • Work with business teams to understand requirements and translate them into SharePoint solutions.
  • Assist in migration projects (On‑Prem to SharePoint Online).
Technical Skills
  • SharePoint Online & SharePoint 2013/2016/2019
  • SPFx (React / TypeScript / JavaScript)
  • HTML, CSS, jQuery
  • CSOM, JSOM, REST API
  • Microsoft Graph API
  • Power Apps & Power Automate
  • Nintex (optional)
  • Azure AD & Authentication
  • Knowledge of site architecture, metadata, governance, and permissions
  • Experience in SharePoint migration tools (ShareGate, Metalogix) is a plus
Preferred Qualifications
  • Microsoft 365 Developer / SharePoint Developer certifications
  • Experience in Agile/Scrum environments
  • Experience with Microsoft Teams app development (optional)
Why Join Us?
  • Work with modern M365 technologies
  • Opportunity to build enterprise-level solutions
  • Supportive work culture and learning opportunities

raw.title: Supplier Quality Engineer - Spacecraft Hardware
raw.excerpt: Please review the job details below. Lanteris Space Systems/Intuitive Machines is seeking a motivated and skilled Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE).
raw.description:
Please review the job details below.

Lanteris Space Systems/Intuitive Machines is seeking a motivated and skilled Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE). In this role, you will become the person accountable for ensuring that the supplier can produce the right product, to the required quality, on the required schedule, and in accordance with the contractual requirements. The position is responsible for the supplier from initial qualification through delivery. The one person having the complete picture, end-to end supplier performance! This is a remote position.


Key Responsibilities

  • Own the overall relationship with assigned suppliers.
  • Establish and track supplier schedule, quality, and delivery performance.
  • Monitor supplier commitments and production readiness.
  • Work with the Supplier to identify and manage supplier risks.
  • Lead supplier performance reviews and executive escalations.
  • Coordinate with Supply Chain and Engineering activities.
  • Ensure suppliers meet contractual, engineering, and quality requirements.
  • Perform supplier assessments and audits, manufacturing and quality processes.
  • Lead supplier corrective actions and root-cause investigations and drive recovery plans when suppliers fall behind.
  • Address nonconformances, escapes, and recurring quality issues.
  • Review first-article/qualification activities and inspection requirements.
  • Monitor quality metrics and drive continuous improvement.

Responsible for the 5 KPIs of the job position

  • Supplier Performance — cost, quality, schedule, delivery
  • Supplier Quality — compliance, audits, NCRs, corrective actions
  • Supplier Development — process improvement and capability
  • Supplier Risk — capacity, technical, manufacturing, and schedule risk
  • Supplier Relationship & Escalation — supplier leadership and internal executive communication

Minimum Qualifications

  • Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Aerospace, Industrial, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, or Supplier Quality within aerospace, space, defense, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of AS9100 quality management requirements and aerospace manufacturing standards.
  • Demonstrated experience leading root cause investigations and corrective actions (RCCA/CAPA) using structured methodologies such as 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, or equivalent.
  • Extensive experience with nonconformance management, Material Review Board (MRB), and disposition of manufacturing issues.
  • Experience performing, reviewing, or approving First Article Inspections (FAI) in accordance with AS9102.
  • Strong ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, BOMs, manufacturing work instructions, and inspection requirements.
  • Experience applying quality tools such as PFMEA/FMEA, SPC, control plans, process capability analysis, risk assessment, and inspection planning.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently resolve complex manufacturing and quality issues throughout the design, production, integration, and test lifecycle.
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, Program Management, and Supplier Quality.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership with the ability to mentor engineers and influence quality and manufacturing decisions across programs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical risks, quality issues, and corrective actions to engineering and program leadership.
  • Must be able to travel outside of the U.S. – 50% travel minimum
  • Must have a home office available
  • Must have reliable transportation

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical discipline.
  • 12+ years of quality engineering experience with significant experience supporting spacecraft, satellite, aerospace, or defense hardware.
  • Experience supporting hardware through prototype, qualification, production, integration, test, and flight delivery.
  • Working knowledge of NASA, DoD, or other government/customer quality requirements.
  • Experience with spaceflight hardware workmanship standards, including IPC/J-STD or NASA workmanship requirements.
  • Experience supporting or leading customer, regulatory, and AS9100 audits.
  • Experience with supplier quality, source inspection, supplier corrective actions, and supplier development.
  • Demonstrated experience driving measurable improvements in first-pass yield, defect reduction, scrap/rework, escapes, and manufacturing process capability.
  • Experience implementing quality requirements for new product introduction (NPI) and transitioning designs into production.
  • ASQ certification such as Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or equivalent is a plus.
  • Experience serving as the technical quality authority for complex aerospace hardware or spacecraft programs.

In support of pay transparency at Lanteris Space Systems, we disclose salary ranges on all U.S. job postings. The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the salary range provided below and is determined based on job-related factors, including, but not limited to, the experience, qualifications, knowledge, skills, geographic work location, and market conditions. Candidates with the minimum necessary experience, qualifications, knowledge, and skillsets for the position should not expect to receive the upper end of the pay range.

● The base pay for this position within Colorado is: $90,000.00 - $150,000.00 annually.● The base pay for this position within New Jersey is: $90,000.00 - $150,000.00 annually.● The base pay for this position within Delaware is: $90,000.00 - $150,000.00 annually.● The base pay for this position within the Washington, DC metropolitan area is: $99,000.00 - $165,000.00 annually.● The base pay for this position within California is: $104,000.00 - $173,000.00 annually.

For all other states, we use geographic cost of labor as an input to develop market-driven ranges for our roles, and as such, each location where we hire may have a different range.


We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off, health and welfare insurance, and 401(k) to eligible employees. More information on our benefits will be shared with candidates as they move forward in the recruitment process.

The application window is three days from the date the job is posted and will remain posted until a qualified candidate has been identified for hire. If the job is reposted regardless of reason, it will remain posted three days from the date the job is reposted and will remain reposted until a qualified candidate has been identified for hire.


The date of posting can be found on the Lanteris Space Systems Career page at the top of each job posting.


To apply, submit your application via the Lanteris Space Systems Career page.

Lanteris Space Systems values diversity in the workplace and is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

raw.description:
Find your calling at Mercy!

The Supervisor for Behavioral Health Call Center is responsible for the coordination and oversight of call center and customer service activity and providing oversight support to the call center team of caregivers. The Supervisor implements, monitors, and reports in key areas promoting efficient functioning of the Call Center department's day-to-day operations. This position leads a department of customer service coworkers and collaborates closely with the department’s leadership team.

Position Details:

Supervisor, Behavioral Health Call Center


At Mercy, we're committed to delivering compassionate care and exceptional service to every patient, every day. As a Supervisor, Behavioral Health Call Center, you will play a vital role in ensuring individuals seeking behavioral health services receive timely support, guidance, and access to care. This position combines leadership, operations, and customer service expertise to help drive positive outcomes for the communities we serve.

The Supervisor is responsible for the coordination, oversight, and performance of the Behavioral Health and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Call Center. This leader will manage a team of customer service caregivers, monitor key quality and operational metrics, and partner closely with Behavioral Health and EAP leadership to support Mercy's mission of bringing healing ministry and compassionate care to those in need.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the daily operations of the Behavioral Health and EAP Call Center, ensuring exceptional service and efficient workflows.
  • Recruit, hire, train, coach, and develop a high-performing team of customer service caregivers.
  • Manage caregiver scheduling, staffing coverage, and timekeeping processes.
  • Monitor call center performance through quality audits, performance reviews, and operational reporting.
  • Analyze key metrics and trends to drive continuous improvement, efficiency, and service excellence.
  • Collaborate closely with Behavioral Health, EAP, and organizational leadership to support departmental goals.
  • Coordinate with after-hours service vendors to ensure seamless patient access and support.
  • Review, develop, and update call center policies and procedures as needed.
  • Manage customer complaints, concerns, and grievances in partnership with leadership and key stakeholders.
  • Support departmental reporting, account receivable functions, and administrative operations.
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives, accreditation readiness activities, and process enhancement efforts.
  • Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, compassion, and service excellence aligned with Mercy's values.
  • Perform additional non-clinical duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Education

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

Experience

  • Three to five years of experience in a behavioral healthcare environment required.
  • Previous leadership or supervisory experience preferred.
  • Call center supervisory experience strongly preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Behavioral Health, Human Services, or a related field preferred.

Experience

  • Three to five years of experience in managed behavioral healthcare, EAP services, healthcare customer service, or a health-related call center setting.
  • Experience with quality auditing, operational reporting, and accreditation preparation.
  • Experience working with electronic health records (EHRs) and healthcare technology platforms.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications including Outlook, Excel, Word, and Teams.

Our Ideal Candidate

You thrive in a fast-paced healthcare environment and are passionate about supporting both patients and caregivers. You're a collaborative leader who values service excellence, embraces continuous improvement, and enjoys helping teams succeed while making a meaningful difference in the lives of others.

Why Mercy?

At Mercy, we believe healthcare is a calling. We are one of the nation's leading health systems, serving communities through a mission-driven culture focused on compassion, excellence, dignity, justice, service, and stewardship. As a Mercy caregiver, you'll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact while working alongside a team dedicated to helping people live healthier lives.

Join Mercy and help ensure patients receive the support, access, and compassionate care they deserve from their very first call. ❤️

Why Mercy?

From day one, Mercy offers outstanding benefits - including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, tuition support, and matched retirement plans for team members working 32+ hours per pay period.

Join a caring, collaborative team where your voice matters. At Mercy, you'll help shape the future of healthcare through innovation, technology, and compassion. As we grow, you'll grow with us.

Symetra has an exciting opportunity to join our team as an Actuarial Associate I or II!

About the Role

This role is responsible for running the monthly fixed indexed annuity valuation model, ensuring timely and accurate financial results. The actuary will also develop and implement model enhancements and perform in‑depth analyses to support business insights and process improvements.

What you will do

  • Assists with product development, financial reporting, management reporting, experience studies, and actuarial research.
  • May prepare reports, maintain spreadsheets, databases, and other actuarial software.
  • Commitment to self development, attaining industry knowledge, and passing actuarial exams to achieve actuarial designation.

Why work at Symetra

"Symetra will spoil you. There aren't many companies that will put as much effort into you being a success as Symetra. The culture will challenge you but simultaneously put you at ease. Failure is seen as integral to the learning process so there is less reason to be fearful of it." - Kerry S., Sr. Systems Analyst

“I feel welcome and included at Symetra every day and I really believe you can be you at Symetra." - Megan H., Deputy Chief Compliance Officer

What we offer you

We don’t take a “one-size-fits-all” approach when it comes to our employees. Our programs are designed to make your life better both at work and at home.

  • Flexible full-time or hybrid telecommuting arrangements
  • Plan for your future with our 401(k) plan and take advantage of immediate vesting and company matching up to 6%
  • Paid time away including vacation and sick time, flex days and ten paid holidays
  • Give back to your community and double your impact through our company matching
  • Want more details? Check out our Symetra Benefits Overview

Compensation

Salary Range:$75,000-$119,000 dependent on experience,plus eligibility for annual bonus programs

Who you are

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent with strong quantitative background including college level mathematics.
  • 1 to 3 years of annuity related actuarial experience.
  • 1 to 3 actuarial exams.
  • Proven ability to adhere to due dates and strong sense of accountability.
  • Has a basic understanding of annuity products.
  • Ability to work collaboratively.
  • Preferred experience with Python, SQL/Snowflake and or other actuarial modeling software.
  • High school diploma required.
We empower inclusion
At Symetra, we aspire to be the most inclusive insurance company in the country. We're building a place where every employee feels valued, respected, and has opportunities to contribute.
Inclusion is about recognizing our assumptions, considering multiple perspective, and removing barriers. We accept and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives, because lifting each other up fuels thought and builds a stronger, more innovative company. We invite you to learn more about our efforts here.
Creating a world where more people have access to financial freedom
Symetra is a national financial services company dedicated to helping people achieve their financial goals and feel confident about the future. In our daily work, we're guided by the principles of Value, Transparency and Sustainability. This means we provide products and services people need at a competitive price, we communicate clearly and openly so people understand what they're buying, and we design products--and operate our company--to stand the test of time. We're committed to showing up for our communities, lifting up our employees, and standing up for diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI). Join our team and help us create a world where more people have access to financial freedom.
For more information about our careers visit:
Work Authorization
Employer work visa sponsorship and support are not provided for this role. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States at hire and must maintain authorization to work in the United States throughout their employment with our company.
Please review Symetra's Remote Network Minimum Requirements:
As a remote-first organization with a cameras-on culture, reliable internet connectivity is important to how we connect, collaborate, and serve our customers. To support a positive experience for both employees and customers, Symetra has the following standards for employees' internet connection:
  • Minimum Internet Speed:100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload, in alignment with the FCC's definition of "broadband."
  • Internet Type:Fiber, Cable (e.g., Comcast, Spectrum), or DSL.
  • Not Permissible:Satellite (e.g., Starlink), cellular broadband (hotspot or otherwise), any other wireless technology, or wired dial-up.
When applying to jobs at Symetra you'll be asked to test your internet speed and confirm that your internet connection meets or exceeds Symetra's standard as outlined above.

Identity Verification

Symetra is committed to fair and secure hiring practices. For all roles, candidates will be required (after the initial phone screen) to be on video for all interviews. Symetra will take affirmative steps at key points in the process to verify that a candidate is not seeking employment fraudulently, e.g. through use of a false identity.
Failure to comply with verification procedures may result in:
  • Disqualification from the recruitment process
  • Withdrawal of a job offer
  • Termination of employment and other criminal and/or civil remedies, if fraud is discovered
